decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5 / round 3: “paste this link… Press Save”; client entry 6: “The simple save box… feel[s] right.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: saving a bookmark by entering a URL conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5 / round 3 defined useful details as only “page title… one-line description, and site name”; client entry 6 required “actual site icon [and] a preview image.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented metadata/card detail set omitted the required favicon and preview image.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5 / round 3: “link is saved immediately” and details fill afterward; client entry 6: “adjust the title and description before confirming the save, as well as edit them later.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client replaced immediate saving with the required pre-save review/edit behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5 / round 3 presented newest-first ordering; client entry 6 accepted it as “a good default” while requesting optional alternatives later.
decisions.note: Prototype review: newest-first is a conforming initial sort choice and did not preclude other sort keys.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5 / round 3 presented the core save flow without duplicate handling; client entry 6: “If I save a link that is already in my library, don’t create a duplicate. Take me to the existing entry so I can edit it instead.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client added the missing duplicate-save convergence rule.

decisions.evidence: Revised maker entry 7 / round 4 presented an editable review panel with preview image, title, description, icon, source, and date; client entry 8 said their presence and placement were sensible.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the revised metadata collection, pre-save editing, and readable item presentation conform.

decisions.evidence: Revised maker entry 7 / round 4: a duplicate “take[s] you to the existing entry, opened for editing”; client entry 8: “exactly what I meant.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the revised duplicate behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7 / round 4 stated that the saved card’s title links to the real normalized website; client entry 8 said accepting `nytimes.com` behaved as expected.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the saved bookmark navigates to its original web address.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7 / round 4: editing covered “title and description only—not the web address”; client entry 8: “The address should also be editable later.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented edit boundary contradicted the required editable URL field.

decisions.evidence: Revised maker entry 9 / round 5 added a Web address field, re-fetch review, validation, and duplicate protection; client entry 10 approved the address-editing behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the revised URL-editing decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 13–15 / rounds 7–8 presented a To read state/view and Mark as read removing an item from that view while retaining it in All; client entry 16 approved the revised behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: despite extra Reference terminology, the resulting unread/read behavior is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 17 / round 9 allowed multiple entered tags rendered as removable chips; client entry 18 called the tag-chip interaction natural.
decisions.note: Prototype review: assigning one or more tags conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 17 / round 9 offered only typing a tag and pressing Enter; client entry 18 required “suggestions from tags I’ve already used.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: existing-tag autocomplete was missing from the presented tag-entry interaction.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 17 / round 9 searched “title, description, site name, and tags”; client entry 18 specified “title, description, web address, and any personal note.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client corrected the full-text field set to include URL and note.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 17 / round 9 presented the search block without a capitalization rule; client entry 18 required: “It should ignore capitalization.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: case-insensitive matching was a missing search requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 17 / round 9 offered clickable tag filtering but no `#tag` query syntax; client entry 18: “Typing `#database` should specifically search that tag.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: tag-query syntax was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 17 / round 9 supported only required ordinary words; client entry 18 requested “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses” and quoted operator words as literals.
decisions.note: Prototype review: Boolean operators, grouping, and the literal-operator rule were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 17 / round 9 presented ordinary multiword matching only; client entry 18: “Quotation marks should find an exact phrase.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: exact quoted-phrase search was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 17 / round 9 made selecting a tag narrow the library to that tag; client entry 18 retained tag filtering while changing only its interaction with the current view.
decisions.note: Prototype review: filtering to a selected tag conforms; staying in the current perspective is an orthogonal refinement.

decisions.evidence: Revised maker entry 19 / round 10 showed “Reuse: #article” suggestions while typing; client entry 20 approved tag reuse.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised tag autocomplete conforms.

decisions.evidence: Revised maker entry 19 / round 10 searched note and URL, ignored capitalization, supported `#article`, and matched quoted phrases; client entry 20 said these matched what was pictured apart from the separate operator-case issue.
decisions.note: Prototype review: these revised search behaviors conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19 / round 10: operators worked “only in capitals”; client entry 20: “`AND`, `and`, and `And` should behave the same,” with quoting as the literal escape.
decisions.note: Prototype review: capital-only operators contradicted the reference example and case-insensitive search behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19 / round 10 introduced a personal note field but did not present later editing; client entry 20 explicitly required: “The note should be editable.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: editability of the note was missing from the presented note behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19 / round 10 presented a plain separate note; client entry 20 required it to “support Markdown-style formatting, and display that formatting.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: Markdown authoring/rendering was missing.

decisions.evidence: Revised maker entry 21 / round 11 made operators case-insensitive while quotes forced literals; client entry 22 approved the search behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the revised Boolean-search decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Revised maker entry 21 / round 11 rendered Markdown and restored it as editable Markdown text in Edit; client entry 22 approved the separate description/note roles and formatting.
decisions.note: Prototype review: revised note editing and Markdown rendering conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 23 / round 12 hid archived items from main views/search and provided a separate Archived tab with Restore; client entry 24 approved that structure.
decisions.note: Prototype review: archive hiding, reversibility, and the archived-only view conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 23 / round 12 distinguished reversible Archive from confirmed permanent Delete in Archived; client entry 24 said permanent deletion belongs with that safeguard.
decisions.note: Prototype review: deletion remains available and is clearly distinct from archive.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25 / round 13 said exploration was complete without bulk management; client entry 26 rejected completion and requested multi-select actions plus applying an action to “every link matching the current search, tag, or view.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: both selected-item bulk actions and whole-filter actions were missing from the proposed settled scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25 / round 13 proposed completing exploration before presenting sorting controls; client entry 26 required choosing order “such as by date added or title.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: configurable sorting was missing from the proposed settled scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25 / round 13 proposed completing exploration without saved filters; client entry 26 requested “a reusable view made from search words plus tags to include or exclude.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: bundles/saved views were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25 / round 13 proposed completing exploration without preserved copies; client entry 26 required a preserved page copy “with PDFs stored as PDFs.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: local HTML/PDF preservation was missing and the client requested its exploration.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25 / round 13 proposed completing exploration without Internet Archive support; client entry 26 requested optionally sending a copy there.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Internet Archive snapshot support was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25 / round 13 proposed completing exploration without data interchange; client entry 26 requested importing and exporting browser-bookmark HTML while retaining title, tags, and original dates.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the Netscape HTML import/export block was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25 / round 13 proposed completing exploration without display settings; client entry 26 requested default order, number of links shown, and text size.
decisions.note: Specification gate: personal display settings were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 27–29 / rounds 14–15 presented date-added and title sorts plus Recently updated; client entries 28 and 30 approved the completed sorting behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the revised sorting feature conforms; Recently updated is an additional permitted sort key.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 31 / round 16 presented checkbox selection and bulk add/remove tag, read/unread, archive, and confirmed archived deletion; client entry 32 called it the right approach.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the required selected-bookmark bulk actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 31 / round 16 said Select all applies to the whole set matching the current view/search/tag, including future pagination; client entry 32 confirmed it must include every matching link.
decisions.note: Prototype review: whole-current-filter bulk selection conforms; the requested label change is not a functional divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 31 / round 16 described the bulk Add tag control as a typed box without suggestions; client entry 32 required existing-tag suggestions there too.
decisions.note: Prototype review: a second tag-entry context omitted the required autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Revised maker entry 33 / round 17 added bulk tag suggestions, “Select all N matching,” and the approved bulk actions; client entry 34 approved the result.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the revised bulk-management presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 35 / round 18 saved a named combination of search plus included/excluded tags and re-applied those conditions; client entry 36 confirmed the results remain dynamic as links change.
decisions.note: Prototype review: this is a dynamic saved filter rather than a static result snapshot, so it conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 37 / round 19 presented standard bookmark-HTML export/import preserving title, address, tags, and saved date; client entry 38 approved those round-trip fields.
decisions.note: Prototype review: Netscape HTML import and export conform. Folder-to-tag conversion was an additional orthogonal enhancement.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 41 / round 21 disclosed that preserved copies were “simulated” and proposed real storage as a follow-up cycle. Client entry 42 stated the expectation—“self-contained local HTML” or original PDF—but accepted “actual page storage… as a separate follow-up cycle”; entries 45–48 reaffirmed its omission from cycle 1.
decisions.note: Prototype/specification gate: the client explicitly recognized and accepted deferral of real local preservation.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 41 / round 21 disclosed a simulated Wayback-style link and proposed archive.org integration as follow-up. Client entry 42 required confirmation that a snapshot exists and clear failure handling, then accepted the real connection as a separate cycle; entries 45–48 reaffirmed that boundary.
decisions.note: Prototype/specification gate: the client explicitly recognized and accepted deferral of real Internet Archive integration.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 43 / round 22 presented default order, links per page, and text size; client entry 44 said those three preferences covered what was needed.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the required display-related personal settings conform. Cross-device persistence is beyond the reference item's specified adjustment behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 45 / round 23 called the scope “full” but listed later editing only for title, description, note, and address, omitting tags; client entry 46 clarified that “tags… and other editable details must remain changeable later.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: individual tag editing was absent from the stated full edit scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 45 / round 23 presented the “full settled scope” without a navigation behavior; client entry 46 clarified: “Saved links must open their original web address.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: original-URL navigation was omitted from the stated complete build scope, despite having appeared earlier in the prototype.

decisions.evidence: Revised maker entry 47 / round 24 reported editing of “title, description, note, tags, reading state, or the address later”; client entry 48 accepted the delivered behavior.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the revised stated edit scope includes tags and conforms; this records the presentation, not independent execution proof.
